full_judgment: The questions where the prosecution has not came forward with any evidence at all to substantiate the charge against the accused, what the court is require to do In such a circumstance, whether the learned Additional Sessions Judge would be entitled to pass the order of acquittal under section 265H. In this connection, Mr. Azizur Rahman Chowdhury the learned Advocate for the opposite party, has referred to the case of Md. Taheruddin, Vs. Abul Kashem and others, reported in B.L.D. 1985 page 144 (Vol-V) wherein the learned Judges ware of the opinion that the court of Sessions after framing of the charge could acquit the accused only after all processes for completing the attendance of the prosecution witnesses have been exhausted. The relevant portion of the said decision reads as follows : "It is only when the Sessions Court exhausts all the processes that it acquires the right of recording an order of acquittal in substantial compliance with the provisions of section 365H Cr.P.C."
